title: Aftercare Once You Fly Home: Coordinating Follow-Up From Abroad
seoTitle: Medical Aftercare Abroad: Follow-Up After Türkiye
metaDescription: Coordinate medical aftercare after flying home from Türkiye: remote follow-up, full English discharge files, GP suture care, and complications.
quickAnswer: Safe medical aftercare after leaving Türkiye starts before your return flight. Collect a complete English discharge file—including operative notes, implant serial numbers, and prescriptions—agree on scheduled remote check-ins with your surgical team, and brief your home GP before travel so local wound care or urgent assessment runs smoothly.
category: Medical Travel to Türkiye — Independent Advisory & Safety (The ITO Standard)

body.text: How should remote follow-up with your Turkish surgical team be structured?

Remote aftercare works best when dates, communication channels, and response windows are agreed in writing before you leave the hospital. Rather than relying on ad-hoc chat messages with a sales coordinator, confirm who reviews clinical photos or lab results and how quickly a physician responds if symptoms change.

Public health guidance in the [CDC Yellow Book chapter on medical tourism](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/health-care-abroad/medical-tourism.html) stresses arranging follow-up care before departure and confirming whether remote check-ins carry extra fees. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. Ask for a written timeline—typically day 14, month one, month three, and month six—listing which clinician reviews each milestone and what warning signs require immediate local care.
What full medical discharge file (operative note, implant brands, prescriptions) must you bring home?

Never leave your hospital or clinic with only a brief payment receipt. Both the [NHS treatment abroad checklist](https://www.nhs.uk/using-the-nhs/healthcare-abroad/going-abroad-for-treatment/treatment-abroad-checklist/) and [NaTHNaC TravelHealthPro medical tourism guidance](https://travelhealthpro.org.uk/factsheets/travelling-for-treatment-medical-tourism) emphasise carrying complete English clinical documentation so any doctor at home can understand exactly what was done.

Before heading to the airport—alongside your [Fit-to-Fly certificate](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/flying-after-surgery-turkey)—verify that your physical and PDF discharge packet contains every item below:

items: English discharge summary (Epikriz): Admission and discharge dates, diagnosis, procedures performed, and post-operative course.
Operative note and anaesthesia record: Surgical technique, sutures used (dissolvable or non-dissolvable), and medications given during surgery.
Implant and device passports: Manufacturer, brand, model, lot, and serial stickers for dental implants, breast implants, orthopaedic hardware, or intraocular lenses.
Diagnostic imaging and lab results: Digital copies (DICOM/PDF) of pre- and post-op blood tests, X-rays, or scans.
Prescriptions and generic drug names: Active pharmaceutical ingredients (not only Turkish brand names), dosages, and stop dates.
Signed itemized invoice: Official clinic receipt, as detailed in our [paying for medical treatment in Türkiye guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/paying-for-medical-treatment-turkey).

body.text: How do you arrange local GP or nurse suture removal at home if needed?

Home-country public health systems and family doctors are not obligated to perform routine aftercare for private elective procedures carried out abroad. The [NHS guide to going abroad for medical treatment](https://www.nhs.uk/using-the-nhs/healthcare-abroad/going-abroad-for-treatment/going-abroad-for-medical-treatment/) advises speaking with your GP, dentist, or clinician before travelling to clarify what local follow-up they can or cannot provide.

body.text: What happens if a complication arises after returning home?

If you develop fever, spreading redness, severe pain, shortness of breath, or calf swelling after returning home, seek urgent medical care locally first rather than waiting for an overseas message. As [GOV.UK health advice for Türkiye](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health) and [U.S. Embassy Türkiye medical tourism guidance](https://tr.usembassy.gov/medical-tourism/) note, standard travel insurance rarely covers elective-surgery complications, so check specialist medical-travel complication cover beforehand.

Ask your Turkish provider before booking what their written revision policy covers—and what remains your responsibility, such as return flights and hotels. faq.q: Will my local GP remove stitches from surgery done in Türkiye?
faq.a: Not always. Many GPs and public clinics decline routine aftercare for private overseas procedures. Ask your GP before travelling, or pre-book a private local nurse or walk-in clinic.

faq.q: Why do I need generic medication names on my Turkish discharge sheet?
faq.a: Turkish pharmacy brand names often differ from brands sold in the UK, EU, or US. Generic active-ingredient names let your home doctor or pharmacist check interactions accurately.

faq.q: Should I tell my home doctor before travelling to Türkiye for treatment?
faq.a: Yes. Official NHS and CDC guidance recommends informing your GP or specialist before travelling so they can review your baseline health and advise on safe local follow-up.

faq.q: What if a clinic refuses to give me my operative notes in English?
faq.a: You are entitled to your medical records under Turkish patient rights and KVKK rules. Confirm English discharge documentation in writing before paying any deposit.

faq.q: Does regular travel insurance cover complications after elective surgery abroad?
faq.a: Standard holiday travel insurance almost always excludes complications arising from planned overseas medical or cosmetic procedures. Look for dedicated medical-travel complication insurance if available in your country.

faq.q: Can Itinerary of Türkiye chase missing discharge paperwork for me?
faq.a: We help clients establish document checklists before admission and coordinate practical communication while you are in Türkiye. Clinical records and medical decisions always remain between you and your licensed hospital.
